Widen the orchestration test bounds that host load can exceed (#284)

TODO 254 records that the tests that give a normally ending enumerator
a 5 second timeout were not swept for load sensitivity, and that under
host load the timeout could cut short a child that should end
normally. The hook starts the enumerator's timeout clock when it
starts the child (subprocess.run at aiqt_hooks.py:22833), so that
timeout also covers interpreter start-up. This closes TODO 254.

tools/test-orch-stage2-hooks.py:

- ENUM_TIMEOUT, 60 seconds, the hook's own fallback
  (aiqt_hooks.py:22831), replaces 5 at the 3 fixture registries whose
  enumerator should end normally: stage2(), _arm_writing_enumerator
  and the doctor disclosure case. The 2 registries whose argv is
  malformed by design keep 5, since no child starts there.
- RUN_TIMEOUT, 120 seconds, bounds each test run that can start the
  enumerator of a fixture registry once: run_hook, run_doctor, the 2
  direct preflight runs, Doctor.SPECIAL_TIMEOUT (was 30),
  DoctorCheckpointWrites.TIMEOUT (was 30) and the new
  DoctorStandInRestore.TIMEOUT (was 60). The fault-injection run of
  DoctorCheckpointWrites can start it twice and keeps twice the bound,
  240 seconds. So every test bound around such a run is at least 120
  seconds, and each exceeds ENUM_TIMEOUT, once for each enumerator run
  it can hold, by at least ENUM_MARGIN, 60 seconds, so the hook's own
  timeout ends an enumerator that hangs before a test bound ends the
  run.
- run_doctor_recorded, the 1 launcher of the suite, holds the timeout
  that each launch was given, however the case bound it, to the
  enumerator starts that the launch recorded. It names a new file of the
  launch's own in ORCH_STAGE2_ENUMERATOR_RUNS in the launch's
  environment, and every enumerator that a case declares through
  write_registry first runs ENUM_RUN_MARK, which adds 1 line to that
  file. However the launch ends, the recorder counts the lines, and a
  launch whose timeout is under ENUM_TIMEOUT for each start plus
  ENUM_MARGIN fails its case in its cleanup, while any exception that
  the launch raised goes on to the case unchanged. With no case
  running, the launch fails at once instead, with any exception that
  the launch raised as the cause, also when the launch printed a
  doctor refusal as well, whose failed registration is then the
  context. A launch with no start, or with no timeout, is not held.
- Stage2Harness.write_registry checks the declared enumerator as the
  hook reads it, from the JSON text that it writes, so a tuple is
  checked as the list that json writes and a str subclass as its
  text, in 1 place, declared_enumerator_defect. It accepts an
  enumerator that the hook would start only when its argv is exactly
  this interpreter (sys.executable), -I, -c and 1 of ENUM_PROGRAMS,
  each a separate element, and when its timeout, as the hook reads
  it, is at most ENUM_TIMEOUT. ENUM_PROGRAMS holds ENUM_FIXTURE,
  WRITING_ENUM_FIXTURE and SLEEPING_ENUM_FIXTURE, the sleeping
  enumerator of the enumerator timeout case. Each begins with
  ENUM_RUN_MARK and compiles, and after the mark it names neither the
  record nor the environment and opens, removes or writes no path but
  its own operands. The program is the argv element itself, so the
  check reads the text that the interpreter compiles; no file is
  read. It refuses every other shape, including every other program
  and every program file: a check of a program's text cannot see
  every way in which the program could reach the record, and what the
  interpreter runs for a file operand depends on the operand's name
  and content, on how the path resolves, and on the file at each run,
  not only on the text that a check reads. It refuses some
  enumerators that record their start and leave the record alone,
  such as a program file that begins with the mark or any program
  outside ENUM_PROGRAMS; each refusal fails safe.
- Every fixture enumerator is declared in that form, with ENUM_FIXTURE
  or WRITING_ENUM_FIXTURE as the program, so the backlog moves from
  argv[3] to argv[4], and the doctor operand label that the cases
  check moves with it; the fixture program file of setUp is removed.
  This suite no longer drives a program-file enumerator through the
  hook: apart from requiring a list of non-empty strings, the hook
  passes the argv to subprocess.run unchanged (aiqt_hooks.py:22833),
  so the hook behaviour under test does not depend on its form. The
  doctor's operand pre-check does: it checks each element from
  argv[2] on as a path, as for a committed registry, whose argv[2] the
  registry gate requires to be a script, so for these registries it
  also checks -c and the program, and it refuses a special file at
  <root>/-c, running no enumerator, where the hook runs the
  enumerator. A new Doctor case pins that refusal. The project's own
  file enumerator keeps its own suite.
- EnumeratorBounds requires that a stage-2 Stop and preflight each
  record 1 start and a stage-1 Stop none; that a launch 1 second under
  its bound fails its case and a launch at its bound passes, for 1
  start and for 2, also when check=True fails, and that one with no
  running case fails at once, with the launch's exception as the
  cause, also when it printed a doctor refusal as well; that each of
  ENUM_PROGRAMS begins with the record and names neither the record
  nor the environment after it, and that the 2 fixture programs that
  end each record exactly 1 start through the hook; that
  write_registry refuses a -c enumerator without the record, a tuple
  argv, a str subclass that json writes as -cpass, a joined -cpass or
  -Ic, -c before -I, another option in place of -I, an option between
  -I and -c, a program that begins with the record and then removes
  it, adds a start, opens the file that the environment names or
  removes the record that it finds by the name of its folder, one
  that holds the record only as text or after an exit, one that
  begins with it but does not compile, one run without -I or by
  another interpreter, and a timeout over ENUM_TIMEOUT; and that it
  refuses each program-file form found so far, each with a recording
  file in place: a plain file, a relative file under the root, -u, --
  or - before the file, a directory, a .pyc name and a trailing slash.
- DoctorCheckpointWrites._doctor drops a timeout parameter that no
  caller passes.
- In the enumerator timeout case the bound on the hook run goes from
  15 to 90 seconds and the sleep of its enumerator from 30 to 100
  seconds, so a hook that waited the sleep out still fails the case.

tools/test-orch-enumerate-backlog.py:

- ENUMERATE_PROG runs the real enumerator under a 60 second timeout
  instead of 5.
- The new case test_hook_ends_an_enumerator_that_does_not_end runs a
  90 second sleep through ENUMERATE_PROG under a 120 second bound and
  requires ENUMERATOR_ERROR with "timed out after 60 seconds".
- The stamp test, renamed
  test_generated_at_utc_is_stamped_while_the_enumerator_runs, requires
  that the stamp lie between the clock before the run, truncated to
  the second, and the clock after it. The enumerator truncates its
  stamp to whole seconds, so the lower bound is exact, and the test
  refuses a stale stamp that the old window accepted.
- InputFileType.TIMEOUT, ErrorPosition.TIMEOUT and
  RuntimeGuard.TIMEOUT, the bounds on each enumerator run of those
  classes, go from 20 to 60 seconds, the timeout ENUMERATE_PROG gives
  the enumerator, and the failure message of InputFileType says only
  that the enumerator did not exit within that bound.

tools/test-orchestration-registry.py: SpecialFileInputs.TIMEOUT, the
bound on each gate run of that class, start-up included, replaces the
literal 20 with 60 seconds, and its failure message says only that the
gate did not exit within that bound, not that it blocked on a special
file. The timeouts of 5 in the suite's registries do not change: they
are data that the registry gate checks, no child runs under them, and
the gate refuses any timeout outside (0, 8]. The test registries of
the stage-2 and enumerate-backlog suites never reach the gate.

tools/test-orch-migrate-todo.py: InputFileType.TIMEOUT,
ErrorPosition.TIMEOUT and RuntimeGuard.TIMEOUT, the bounds on each
migration run of those classes, start-up included, go from 20 to 60
seconds, and the failure message of InputFileType says only that the
migration did not exit within that bound, not that the open blocked.

Checks, run from the repository root with python3 -I: the stage-2,
enumerate-backlog, registry and migrate-todo suites each end OK, and
the label suite ends OK in a git checkout. With 1 edit in a copy of
the tree, a 6 s start-up delay of the fixture enumerator, on a line
before its import json line, which with this change follows
ENUM_RUN_MARK, fails 4 stage-2 cases on main's test files and none
with this change; a 6 s delay of the real enumerator fails the hook
case and the stamp test on main's files and neither with this change;
a 21 s delay of the real enumerator fails the large-input
InputFileType case on main's files and not with this change, and a
61 s delay fails it with this change; the same 21 s delay fails 2
ErrorPosition and 2 RuntimeGuard cases at their 20 s bounds on main's
files and none with this change, and a 61 s delay fails
ErrorPosition.test_missing_input with this change; a 50 s delay of the
hook fails the enumerator timeout case's old 15 s bound and passes its
90 s bound. A 21 s start-up delay of the registry gate fails the 3
SpecialFileInputs cases at their 20 s bound on main's files and none
with this change, and a 61 s delay fails
test_fifo_registry_fails_promptly at its 60 s bound. A 21 s start-up
delay of the migration fails 1 case of each of InputFileType,
ErrorPosition and RuntimeGuard in the migrate-todo suite at its 20 s
bound on main's files and none with this change, and a 61 s delay
fails all 3 at their 60 s bound. Controls: a 91 s hook delay fails the
90 s bound, an enumerator stamp 3 s stale fails the new stamp test,
and a 100 s timeout in ENUMERATE_PROG fails the new hang case. With
this change, a new Doctor case whose preflight launch has a timeout of
30, through a local RUN_TIMEOUT, through an alias of
run_doctor_recorded with a mapping, or in a class outside the harness,
fails, and passes with RUN_TIMEOUT; DoctorStandInRestore fails with
self.TIMEOUT set to 30 before its launch, and the planted-module case
fails with the bounds of its 2 launches swapped. A new Doctor case
that declares a -c enumerator holding ENUM_RUN_MARK only as text fails
at write_registry, and with the fixture enumerator fails its timeout
of 30. A new case whose launch with a timeout of 119 starts the
fixture enumerator once and then fails check=True errors with that
CalledProcessError and fails in its cleanup with a failure that has no
cause. EnumeratorBounds fails when the check never reports, drops
ENUM_MARGIN or ignores the number of starts, when the recorder names
the file in another variable, when write_registry skips its check,
checks the object that it is given rather than the text read back,
takes any interpreter, does not compare argv[1] or argv[2], accepts
any program that begins with the record, with or without the name
check, or also accepts a recording program file, when the name check
finds nothing, when ENUM_FIXTURE lacks ENUM_RUN_MARK, and when the
failure with no running case drops its cause or takes the failed
registration of a doctor refusal as its cause. The new doctor case
fails when the doctor skips an argv element that is exactly -c. With
a fixture enumerator that sleeps 70 s, from the same line as the 6 s
delay, neither the present-marker case of DoctorCheckpointWrites nor
the DoctorStandInRestore case ends through a test bound, on main or
with this change; with this change and the earlier bounds, each does.
With 64 busy processes and the enumerator timeout case pinned to 1
CPU, the case is expected to end OK in each of 3 runs.

Residuals: a wider bound makes a load failure rarer, not impossible.
An enumerator that hangs holds a test run for up to 60 s, a doctor or
hook run that blocks fails after 120 s instead of 30, and an
enumerator run of InputFileType, ErrorPosition or RuntimeGuard, a gate
run of SpecialFileInputs, or a migration run of InputFileType,
ErrorPosition or RuntimeGuard in the migrate-todo suite, that blocks
fails after 60 s instead of 20. The new hang case adds 60 s to the
enumerate-backlog suite. The bound check counts only starts that an
enumerator records. The record is a file that any process of this
user can write, so its count rests on reading the 3 programs of
ENUM_PROGRAMS, and a program that the launcher starts directly is
trusted as the suite's own code is. Code that the interpreter runs
before any program under -I (site: .pth import lines and
sitecustomize) and a registry written other than through
write_registry are not seen, and a child that drops
ORCH_STAGE2_ENUMERATOR_RUNS from its environment and a start that
ends before its program runs are not counted. It holds only the
starts a launch made when a case ran it, not a start recorded after
the launch returned, and not a launch with no timeout. The doctor
refuses a special file at <root>/-c for the -c registries of the
stage-2 suite, where the hook runs the enumerator; the refusal runs no
enumerator, a registry that the gate accepts never has -c at argv[2],
and changing the doctor's operand model is product work outside this
change. The fixture value 60 is safe only while the test registries
are never gated. The new stamp test fails on a backward clock step
during the run. The load check covers only the enumerator timeout case
and CPU contention.
